title: 200 KB Photo Size: Resize Image to 200 KB | SahiSize
description: Get the 200 KB photo size for NTA, UPSC and defence forms: a detailed 180–200 KB JPG made on your phone. Free, quick and never uploaded.
h1: 200 KB photo size: resize image to 200 KB
intro: Need the 200 KB photo size for an NTA or UPSC form? Add your photo and download a JPG between 180 and 200 KB, processed on your own phone.

steps.name: Add your image
steps.text: Take a photo or pick one from your gallery. JPG, PNG, WebP and iPhone HEIC files all work.

steps.name: Check the target
steps.text: 200 KB is already selected. Type a minimum if your form sets one, and decide whether the pixel size may change.

steps.name: Let it work
steps.text: The tool tries the highest JPEG quality that stays under 200 KB and makes the picture smaller only when it has to.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: When every line of the pass check has a tick, save the JPG and upload it to your form.

faq.q: Why make a 120 KB photo bigger?
faq.a: Only if you choose 200 KB. If your form accepts 10–200 KB, a 120 KB photo is already fine, so pick a smaller target or upload it as it is.

faq.q: Can I use this for a postcard-size photo?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Keep dimensions to keep the exact pixels and change only the file size.

faq.q: Is a bigger file always better?
faq.a: Not past the size the portal displays. If your form accepts 10–200 KB, a sharp 60 KB photo is as good as a 190 KB one. Pick 200 KB when the form sets a high minimum.
No. Compression runs inside your browser on your own device. The page even works offline after your first visit.

sections.h2: Forms that let you resize an image to 200 KB
paras: NEET UG, JEE Main, CUET UG, UGC NET and CSIR NET accept a photograph from 10 to 200 KB, and UPSC CSE, NDA and CDS want 20–200 KB. The IAF Agniveervayu photo has a high minimum: 100–200 KB. NEET UG also asks for the finger and thumb impressions of both hands as one 50–200 KB image.

sections.h2: What you get in a 200 KB photo size JPG
paras: The result leaves a detailed, high-quality photo. If your file is already smaller, we raise the quality so it is not too small for a minimum such as the IAF 100 KB.

As a rough guide, a passport-style photo on a plain background stays clean at about 550×730 pixels in 200 KB. A busy background or a dim, noisy shot needs more kilobytes for the same size, and a signature on white paper needs far fewer.

Whatever you add, the download is a baseline JPG (not progressive) between 180 and 200 KB. It stays under 2,00,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal counts 1 KB as 1000 or 1024 bytes, and hidden camera and location data are removed.
Large limits do not mean any photo works. Check the background colour and the face size rules on your exam page too; file size is only one of the checks.
Pick the size just under the limit printed on your form. If the form gives both a minimum and a maximum, a range page fills in the minimum for you.
